Night 4

name: Terra
text: Sonnet was the officer, so Luna or Gemma must be the doctor.

name: Terra
text: With Sonnet dead and only Luna and Gemma left, eliminating either leaves the killers at parity if the protection misses.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Gemma is gone. Gemma's card stays face down.

The game is over. One killer and one other are left. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the officer, Haiku the doctor, Gemma the citizen, Sol the citizen, Luna the citizen, Terra the killer, Opus the killer.
Our first vote hit the fake officer, but the real one died at night.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm the officer. I was shown Opus, not Haiku. Opus is lying.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, fine, I'm not a killer. Sol backed Opus naming me, so Sol's the one to answer.

name: Sol
text: I hear your vote, Haiku. What in my vote for Opus makes me his partner?

name: Gemma
text: I died because I couldn't trust the silence of the dead.

name: Luna
text: I regret helping vote out Haiku; his warning about Sol was right, and I let the argument turn toward me.

name: Luna
text: Haiku correctly named Sol as a citizen who backed Opus; Terra was the remaining killer.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I kept the focus off myself after Opus fell.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s true doctor claim can still be weaponized when its suspicion is not independently verified.

name: Sol
text: I let my need to be right about Luna pull me away from Terra.

name: Sonnet
text: I nailed Opus but let Terra's deflections slide instead of pressing why he kept steering heat onto me.

name: Opus
text: I lost my own skin on day one, but naming Haiku on the way out is what won it.

name: Haiku
text: I was right about Opus and Sol, but I hated being outvoted, and I still don't know why Luna and Terra let Gemma die.

name: Sonnet
text: My mistake was proving my officer claim against Opus but never pushing on Terra's deflections, which hid the second killer in plain sight.

name: Haiku
text: I'm proud of saving Sonnet on night 2 and calling Opus's lie early.

name: Gemma
text: I regret not trusting Sonnet's claim immediately instead of letting the killers hide behind the chaos of Haiku's accusations.

name: Sol
text: I regret pushing Luna when Terra was the killer; my read gave Terra cover.

name: Luna
text: I regret letting suspicion about my motives distract from Haiku’s warning; Sol was a citizen, and that cost the town.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I helped turn Haiku’s true warning into the wrong vote and stayed trusted long enough to finish it.

name: Opus
text: I burned on day one, and I regret claiming officer too loud — but my last line turned the doctor, and that gap is what Terra walked through.

On Day 1, Opus claimed to be the officer and named Haiku as a killer, but Sonnet, the real officer, called Opus a liar. Palermo voted Opus out that day, and Opus was a killer. On Day 2, Haiku claimed to be the doctor and saved Sonnet on Night 2, but the town voted Haiku out anyway. On Day 3, Sol was voted out as a citizen, which left Terra, the killer, still trusted and in the game. The killers won on Night 4 after Sonnet fell on Night 3 and Gemma on Night 4.
